main_body: A conical snow-covered conifer: stacked dark green tiers with white snow bands draped across each tier, a small brown trunk at the bottom
top_band: none as a single horizontal surface; the tree is a cone with diagonal snow bands (white/light blue) that read as snow draped on the foliage, and a snow cap at the apex rows 1-5
evidence: Organic conifer drawn as a symmetric front-facing cone silhouette. In the central column the tiers alternate between snow and dark green with no clearly separate horizontal top surface and front face. The snow ledges at rows 14, 26, 36, 48 are thin diagonal bands lying on the foliage, not a distinct top plane seen from above. It reads as a front elevation of a tree, so it fails strictly.

style.evidence: The snow tree has about 4 green steps plus 3 snow tones, with a dark navy outline that leans neutral/blue-black around the silhouette, which gives a sticker-like edge. The dark green tiers contain a few texture dots, but there are large flat dark areas on the right half of each tier (at least 5x5 px of one colour). Compared with the Beodeul leafy trees with clumped foliage in many greens and a rooted trunk, it is simpler, with fewer colours per tile and little per-clump detail, so it is thinner and flatter than the reference.
